change.title: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 retires on the Claude API Nov 30, 2026; use claude-sonnet-5-5

tasks.reasoning: Both Anthropic call sites pass a dynamic model_id, so the scan cannot see which Claude models the app offers. The SDK pin (0.21.1) suggests a 2024-era model list, which probably does not include claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, so this is uncertain. The migration agent should search the repo's model definitions, config, env defaults and stored settings for 'claude-sonnet-4-5' and replace any match with 'claude-sonnet-5-5'. Before switching, check that this code does not use disabled thinking or forced tool_choice, which can break on Sonnet 5.5. If no reference exists, close as no-op. After the deadline, a retired model returns errors on every chat request that selects it.

callSites.why: messages.create takes its model from a runtime model_id. If the app's model list or a user setting resolves to claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, requests will fail after retirement.
Same dynamic model_id passed to messages.create for the Anthropic branch.

record.prBody:
## claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 retires on the Claude API Nov 30, 2026; use claude-sonnet-5-5 [Not affected]

### Change

No changes made. A repo-wide search (excluding node_modules, .next and the lockfile) found no reference to claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 or any Sonnet 4.5 ID. The app's model lists in config/provider/anthropic.ts and config/provider/amazon.ts hold only Claude 3, 2.x and Instant IDs. The two call sites take model_id dynamically from those lists.

No files changed.

### Why

The retired model ID is not selectable or hardcoded anywhere in the repo, so the retirement can't cause errors here.

> | November 30, 2026 | `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |

Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Provider validators: none run.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Model IDs stored outside the repo, such as users' saved settings or browser storage, were not checked. They could still hold claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929.
- The build check already failed in the baseline run (Killed, probably out of memory). I did not investigate it.

### Behaviour changes

None intended.

---

change.title: npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too

source.quote: * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

tasks.reasoning:
The repo pins @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.21.1, far behind the new 1.0.0 major. Nothing breaks today, because the old SDK keeps sending 2023-06-01. The upgrade is the move that brings in API version 2026-10-21 and its request restrictions: no temperature/top_p/top_k, the document/citation placement rules, and MessageParam becoming a union that may need type fixes where messages are built. It also brings OTel spans by default. One PR should do the bump and fix everything the bump breaks: TypeScript types on messages, the streaming handling across many intervening releases, and any sampling params. Urgency is low because there is no deadline and the current pin keeps working.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-10-21-api-version-2026-10-21 (api-version): New Claude API version 2026-10-21 (anthropic-version header); SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01. SDK 1.0.0 sends anthropic-version 2026-10-21 by default. The repo only moves to that API version through this SDK upgrade, since 0.21.1 keeps sending 2023-06-01.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`."
- anthropic:2026-10-21-sampling-params-removed (field-removed): In API version 2026-10-21, temperature, top_p and top_k in Messages and Batch requests return 400. Only bites under API version 2026-10-21, which this upgrade adopts. The scanned fields show no temperature/top_p/top_k, but the agent must check that the chat routes do not pass a user temperature setting into messages.create and remove it if they do.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "In `2026-10-21`, a request that sends `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` returns a 400 error, even at the parameter’s default value."
- anthropic:2026-10-21-document-citations-user-assistant-errors (other): In API version 2026-10-21, document blocks in assistant messages and citations on text blocks in user messages return 400. Only applies under API version 2026-10-21. The chat messages look text-only, but the agent should confirm no document blocks are sent in assistant messages and no citations on user text blocks when building the messages array.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "In `2026-10-21`, a request that places a `document` block directly in an `assistant` message returns a 400 error."
- anthropic:2026-10-14-ts-sdk-otel-default (other): TypeScript SDK 0.134.0 auto-creates OpenTelemetry spans and trace headers if a global tracer provider exists (unsure if affects; opt out with openTelemetry:false). Upgrading from 0.21.1 to 1.0.0 crosses 0.134.0. If the app registers a global OpenTelemetry tracer provider (e.g. Vercel/Next instrumentation), the SDK will start emitting spans. Decide whether to opt out with openTelemetry:false as part of the same PR.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "If your app registers a global tracer provider, the SDK will create spans with it after upgrading, and they'll be exported with the rest of your traces."

callSites.why: Uses @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.21.1 messages.create with stream and max_tokens. Moving to 1.0.0 changes the default API version, the MessageParam typing (now a union) and removes the sampling params.
Same messages.create streaming call on the 0.21.1 client. It is affected by the same typing and API-version changes.

+import type Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';
+
+// `ai`'s AnthropicStream is typed against the old SDK's event types, so stream the text deltas directly.
+export function anthropicTextStream(response: AsyncIterable<Anthropic.RawMessageStreamEvent>): ReadableStream<Uint8Array> {
+    const encoder = new TextEncoder();
+    const iterator = response[Symbol.asyncIterator]();
+    return new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
+        async pull(controller) {
+            try {
+                while (true) {
+                    const { done, value } = await iterator.next();
+                    if (done) {
+                        controller.close();
+                        return;
+                    }
+                    if (value.type === 'content_block_delta' && value.delta.type === 'text_delta') {
+                        controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(value.delta.text));
+                        return;
+                    }
+                }
+            } catch (error) {
+                controller.error(error);
+            }
+        },
+        async cancel() {
+            await iterator.return?.();
+        },
+    });
+}

## npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too [Verified]

### Change

Bumped @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.21.1 -> 1.0.0 with pnpm 9 (the lockfile changed only for the SDK and its dependencies). Added utils/provider/anthropic.ts, which turns the SDK's raw stream into a text ReadableStream. Both Anthropic call sites now use it in place of `ai`'s AnthropicStream. Added test/anthropic-sdk.test.mjs. Typecheck, build and the new test pass.
- Sampling params: no temperature/top_p/top_k reach messages.create at either call site.
- Document/citation rules: the messages array is passed through from the client untouched. The repo builds no document blocks or citations.
- MessageParam: `messages` is typed `any[]`, so the union needed no change.
- OpenTelemetry: the repo has no instrumentation or global tracer provider, and the routes run on the edge runtime, so I did not set openTelemetry:false.
- Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs: none are installed, so nothing to move.

Files touched:
- `app/api/chat/messages/anthropic/route.ts`
- `app/api/chat/messages/route.ts`
- `package.json`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- `test/anthropic-sdk.test.mjs`
- `utils/provider/anthropic.ts`

### Why

SDK 1.0.0 types the stream as RawMessageStreamEvent, which `ai` 3.1.17's AnthropicStream does not accept (TS2345 at both call sites). 1.0.0 also sends API version 2026-10-21 by default.

> * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | fail (1) | pass | 0 |
| anthropic-sdk-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- anthropic-sdk-test, added by the agent: `node test/anthropic-sdk.test.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `anthropic-sdk-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The pnpm peer warning that the SDK wants zod ^3.25 (the repo has 3.23.8). The repo does not use the SDK's zod helpers, so I left zod alone.
- The model ids stored in the app's config were not checked against retirements at API version 2026-10-21.
- The stream helper emits only text_delta events. AnthropicStream also handled legacy completion chunks, which the Messages API does not send.
- The streaming output was tested only against a mocked SSE response.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Requests now send anthropic-version 2026-10-21 instead of 2023-06-01.
- Streaming no longer goes through `ai`'s AnthropicStream. It uses a local text-delta stream, and the output text is intended to be the same.
- The previously failing build now passes in the sandbox.

concerns.issue: Line ~90 (and anthropic/route.ts:25) passes client-supplied `messages: any[]` straight into `messages.create`. Because of `any`, the passing `typecheck` cannot show these payloads fit the new `MessageParam` union under API version 2026-10-21. If the frontend sends extra fields (e.g. id/createdAt from `ai`'s useChat) or system-role messages, the new API version may reject them. Nothing tests the real client payload shape.

The test injects a fake `fetch` and canned SSE events. It proves the helper concatenates text deltas and that the SDK sets the `anthropic-version` header locally. It does not prove the live 2026-10-21 API accepts these requests or the configured `model_id` values, or that real stream events (ping, error events, non-text deltas) are handled. A `verified` grade over-states this; needs-review seems more accurate.

`@anthropic-ai/sdk@1.0.0` declares peer `zod: ^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0`, but it is resolved as `1.0.0(zod@3.23.8)`. The peer is marked optional, so this probably only matters if the SDK's zod helpers are imported. Still, it is an unmet peer range that pnpm will warn about. Consider bumping zod or confirming nothing depends on the SDK's zod integration.

There is unrelated resolution churn. `eslint-plugin-import`'s optional `@typescript-eslint/parser` moved from 6.21.0 to 7.5.0, and `eslint-module-utils` gained a new variant. `@types/node@18.19.33` was dropped. The helper replaces `AnthropicStream`, so `ai`'s callbacks and stream-data handling are lost. The routes didn't use them, so output should be identical plain text. Mid-stream errors now surface via `controller.error`, which aborts the HTTP response; it is worth confirming the UI handles that the same way as before. The helper runs in `runtime = 'edge'`; `build` passing suggests the new SDK deps (`@opentelemetry/api`, `standardwebhooks`) bundle for edge, but runtime behaviour on edge isn't exercised.

`build` failed before the change and passes after. It is unclear whether the earlier failure was caused by the SDK mismatch or by something pre-existing. Worth confirming the build log so the pass isn't masking an unrelated change.
